common_name: Harry Witch Hazel (Compact AGM Yellow-Orange Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; give 'Harry' room to develop its naturally rounded, as-wide-as-tall form without crowding.

directions: Harry is a 1988 Belgian selection from Robert de Belder that earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its dependable show of large, mildly fragrant, yellow-orange strap petals set off by a purple calyx in mid- to late winter. Unlike leggier witch hazel cultivars, it matures into a neat, rounded shrub roughly as wide as tall, making it easier to fit into a smaller shaded border. Site it in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil where its bare winter branches are visible from a window, and prune only lightly right after bloom to preserve next year's flower buds. Fall foliage turns attractive orange and red before the shrub goes dormant for its winter display.

common_name: Frederic Witch Hazel (Golden-Orange Red-Sepal Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; because 'Frederic' eventually grows quite large and broad, allow it significantly more lateral room than most witch hazel cultivars.

directions: Frederic, a 2000 introduction from Danny de Belder, is a vigorous, bushy, upright witch hazel that grows notably larger than most intermedia cultivars, eventually reaching small-tree proportions in a shaded border. Its faintly scented, strap-shaped petals open bright yellow-orange with striking red sepals at the base in mid- to late winter, and the dark green summer foliage turns good orange-red tones in fall. Because of its eventual size, give it plenty of room from the start rather than planning to prune it into a smaller footprint. Consistent soil moisture and acidic, humus-rich conditions keep it vigorous and free of stress-related dieback.

common_name: Advent Witch Hazel (Early-Blooming Maroon-Calyx Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant in moist but well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; 'Advent' opens its first flowers unusually early once temperatures climb above about 40°F, so site it somewhere visible from indoors in deep winter.

directions: Introduced by Hillier Nurseries in 1979, Advent is a many-branched, upright witch hazel prized for flowering earlier than most intermedia cultivars, often starting in February or sooner during mild spells. Each small yellow bloom has four curly, strap-like petals with red tips emerging from a distinctive maroon-red calyx, and the petals curl protectively closed during hard freezes before reopening as temperatures moderate. Large, wavy-margined leaves emerge yellow-green, mellow to sage-green through summer, then turn yellow in autumn. Grow it in moist, well-drained soil and prune lightly after flowering only if shaping is needed, since flower buds form on the previous season's growth.

common_name: October Magic Carpet Camellia (Dwarf Spreading Pink Double Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to dappled shade; its very low, spreading habit makes it better suited to mass groundcover plantings than as a hedge.

directions: October Magic Carpet is the most diminutive member of the Southern Living Plant Collection sasanqua series, forming a dense, spreading mat of glossy foliage only 2-3 feet tall but considerably wider, well under the height of older dwarf standards like Shishi-Gashira. In fall the low mound is covered in frilly, medium pink, double flowers with a boss of yellow stamens that draw pollinators late in the season. Its groundcover-like habit suits it to large-scale massing, foundation edges, or low informal hedges rather than screening. Keep soil consistently moist and acidic, and mulch well since its shallow, spreading root system dries out faster than upright sasanqua types.
sources: Southern Living Plant Collection / Plants Nouveau

common_name: October Magic Dawn Camellia (Blush-Pink Rose-Form Reblooming Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil with morning sun and afternoon shade; the columnar, upright habit fits narrow side-yard or foundation spaces better than spreading sasanqua cultivars.

directions: October Magic Dawn is a compact, upright Southern Living Plant Collection sasanqua whose large, rose-form blooms open blush pink and deepen toward the petal edges, giving a two-tone effect reminiscent of a garden rose without the thorns or disease pressure. Its dense, columnar growth habit rarely needs pruning to maintain a tidy shape, making it a low-maintenance choice for narrow planting strips. Flowering runs through fall into the cool season, when few other shrubs offer comparable color in a partly shaded bed. Provide consistently moist, acidic soil and a protective mulch layer, and avoid overhead irrigation late in the day to reduce flower spotting.

common_name: October Magic Inspiration Camellia (White Double Magenta-Edged Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in sun to fairly deep shade; this cultivar tolerates more shade than many sasanquas, making it useful under high canopy where other camellias struggle to flower.

directions: October Magic Inspiration is a patented Southern Living Plant Collection sasanqua notable for double white flowers with a yellow center and striking magenta-edged petals, a color combination unusual among fall-blooming camellias. New spring growth emerges with a purple tint before maturing to glossy green, adding a second season of visual interest. It grows well across a wider light range than most camellias, from full sun to shadier positions, though flowering is heaviest with at least a half day of sun. Water deeply during establishment and dry spells, and prune only right after the fall-to-winter bloom period to avoid cutting off next season's buds.

common_name: October Magic White Shi-Shi Camellia (Dwarf Porcelain-White Formal Double Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; its true-dwarf size, smaller than the classic Shishi-Gashira, suits border edges and containers.

directions: October Magic White Shi-Shi is a Southern Living Plant Collection sasanqua bred as a true dwarf companion to the classic Shishi-Gashira, staying noticeably smaller and denser while producing porcelain-white, formal double blooms from late summer into late winter. Its compact, well-branched form works well massed as a low border, in foundation plantings, or in large containers where a full-size sasanqua would overwhelm the space. Average, well-drained garden soil suits it, though flowering and foliage color are best with consistent moisture and acidic soil pH. Because of its extended bloom window, deadheading spent flowers helps keep the display looking tidy through winter.

common_name: Rose of Autumn Camellia (Vigorous Rose-Pink Semi-Double Hedging Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; its fast, upright growth rate makes it a strong candidate for a flowering privacy hedge in place of ligustrum or holly.

directions: Rose of Autumn arose as an open-pollinated seedling of 'Kanjiro' and is grown as much for its rapid, upright vigor as for its flowers, reaching hedge height faster than most sasanqua cultivars. Large, rose-pink, semi-double blooms with wavy petal edges open in fall and soften to a paler pink as they age, standing out against glossy evergreen foliage. Because of its rapid growth, it can be trained as a tall informal or clipped hedge in a fraction of the time needed for traditional hedging shrubs. Keep soil evenly moist and acidic, and shape lightly after flowering if a formal hedge line is desired.

common_name: Bella Rouge Camellia (Deep Red Ruffled Semi-Double Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; its compact, uniform habit holds a clean shape with little pruning, useful for foundation plantings or low hedges.

directions: Bella Rouge, sold in some catalogs under the earlier trade name 'La Rouge', is a compact sasanqua covered from early fall into winter with deep red, semi-double, ruffled flowers, a saturated color that reads as one of the deepest true reds among fall-blooming camellias. Its uniformly dense, evergreen habit stays smaller and tidier than many older red sasanqua cultivars, holding its shape as a structural accent or low hedge with minimal shearing. Deep green, glossy foliage provides year-round backdrop even outside the bloom season. Give it consistently moist, acidic, well-drained soil and a mulch layer to protect its shallow roots through summer heat.
